_comment: python tools/campaign.py configs      (one headless config per cell)
python tools/campaign.py references   (1800 s path-traced reference per cell)
python tools/campaign.py report       (tables, including the run-to-run noise floor)
Scenes are NOT redeclared here. Their identity, camera state, exposure and tone
curve were frozen for the reconnaissance and must not drift between the two, so
this file points at that manifest and adds only what a campaign has and a recon
does not: arms, protocols, categories, rounds and repeats.
A JOB is (cell, arm, protocol) where a cell is (scene, light type). Categories are
a VIEW over jobs, not a partition of them: K1 and K2 both want veach-ajar under its
own light, and it is measured once. That is why the runner takes the union of what
the enabled categories ask for and the report slices the result afterwards.
'rounds' interleaves: the runner walks every job once per round rather than
finishing a job's images back to back, so thermal drift lands on both arms alike.
'repeats' re-walks the WHOLE grid in fresh processes. That is the only way to get
the between-run spread PLAN_BADAWCZY 10.2 asks for - a confidence interval taken
across images of one process understates it 3-10x on this harness.

curve._comment: PLAN_BADAWCZY 7.9 protocol K. Ten images per point, split across the rounds.

K2._what: effect of light type (P1); the only category where light type is an axis
_directionalDropped: PLAN_BADAWCZY 7.2 asks for three light types here. Directional is not
realizable on either scene and the reason is structural, not a matter of
picking a better direction: a directional source sits at infinity, so a
surface is lit only when the ray back along the beam LEAVES the scene, and
both of these scenes are sealed interiors. Measured 2026-08-30 at 4 s,
mean image brightness against the scene's own light:
veach-ajar  own 0.372  vs  directional 0.0067 at intensity 1280 (55x short,
and already clipping at max 0.96 - four directions tried,
including the emitter-to-room axis and both verticals)
staircase   own 0.2196 vs directional 0.0004 at intensity 100 (550x short)
Raising the intensity to close the gap burns the few lit texels to white long
before the mean moves, so the arms would be compared across a black frame.
Opening an aperture would change the scene, which 7.2 forbids. The category
therefore runs area-emissive vs point, which still varies exactly what it is
about - the spatial distribution of the source, area against delta.
